description: Worked at EDF from 2014 to 2022. Began her career in nuclear within a unit created after the Fukushima disaster to handle severe accident situations at power plants; later specialised in contracts and crisis situations. She resigned from EDF upon her election to the National Assembly.
Appointed spokesperson for Emmanuel Macron's party La Republique en Marche in November 2020, jointly with Prisca Thevenot.

role: Member of the National Assembly (Deputy), Hauts-de-Seine 13th constituency
description: Elected deputy for the 13th constituency of Hauts-de-Seine in June 2022. Served on the National Defence and Armed Forces Committee and the Economic Affairs Committee, and was a member of the Parliamentary Office for the Evaluation of Scientific and Technological Choices (OPECST). Seat ended in October 2024 on entering the Barnier government (replaced by her substitute).
Appointed spokesperson of the Government in the Barnier government, succeeding Prisca Thevenot. Left office when the Barnier government fell in December 2024 (succeeded by Sophie Primas).

role: Member of the National Assembly (Deputy), Hauts-de-Seine 13th constituency
description: Returned to the National Assembly as deputy for the 13th constituency of Hauts-de-Seine on 5 December 2024 following the fall of the Barnier government (re-elected in the 2024 snap legislative election). Member of the Ensemble pour la Republique group.
Reappointed spokesperson of the Government in the Lecornu government from 12 October 2025, succeeding Aurore Berge.

role: Minister-Delegate to the Prime Minister, Government spokesperson, in charge of Energy
description: Following the 26 February 2026 reshuffle, appointed Minister-Delegate to the Prime Minister, Government spokesperson, in charge of Energy (under the Minister of the Economy, Finance and industrial, energy and digital Sovereignty). Tasked with leading the major electrification-of-uses plan following adoption of the third multiannual energy programme (PPE 3).
